newsitem.title: UK: Ban tobacco advertising, EU minister urges states.
newsitem.headline: Ban tobacco advertising, EU minister urges states.

text.p: All European Union states should ban tobacco advertising and act to limit smoking in any way they can, European Union social affairs commissioner Padraig Flynn said on Monday.
Flynn told a "smoking summit" in London that governments had to act in concert to stop the 500,000 deaths every year in Europe from tobacco-related disease.

"I firmly believe that it is incumbent on the public health authorities to make the fight against tobacco a priority for action," Flynn told the health officials, doctors, business executives and experts from abroad who gathered to help thr new British government shape its smoking policy.
Smoking targeted the poor, and was one of the biggest reasons for the health gap between rich and poor in Europe, Flynn said.
"The industry has been organised on an international basis for many years. It is now time for governments to act in a similarly concerted way," Flynn added.
"If not, we will soon find that our citizens will be targeted by new marketing efforts in a bid to recover lost markets in the United States and elsewhere."
As an urgent matter EU members should look at the effects of a pending deal under which tobacco companies will pay $368 billion to head off a wave of litigation in U.S. states, he said.
They should also remove incentives to smoke, he added.
"This means that the promotion of tobacco, by direct or indirect advertising, must be removed. There can be no continued justification for pushing sales of such an addictive and deadly product."
Warnings on packets should be strengthened, and the EU should explore the possibility of legally requiring a reduction of tar and nicotine in cigarettes.
"While many argue that smoking is a matter of personal choice, I would add that the addictive properties of tobacco render that choice a dependency," he said.

"The (EU) member states can also adopt a series of measures at national level to reduce smoking: particularly important here would be measures to outlaw sales to minors, to restrict vending machine sales, to improve smoking cessation programmes and to increase taxes on tobacco," Flynn said, praising Britain's Labour government for raising cigarette taxes.
"I will continue to encourage other member states to follow the UK example in raising the real price of cigarettes," he added.
Britain's Health Secretary Frank Dobson said a consultation paper would be issued after the conference.
"But then the talking will have to stop. We will take the action we judge is necessary to stop the scourge of smoking," he said.
Dobson said the government would also press to end tobacco sponsorship of sports and the arts and would help find alternative funding for them.
Britain said on Monday that 61 percent of the British public backed an advertising ban and 69 percent of smokers wanted to quit.

Another batch of statistics released on Monday showed smoking had increased slightly among British teenagers, with 13 per cent of secondary school children aged 11 to 15 smoking at least one cigarette a week.
